Not enough data to judge. Most stars arrived with the launch, and timing alone
cannot tell a launch from a star campaign. The accounts were not checked
(--no-archive). It has 4 forks, and 0 issues and pull requests were opened in
the last 90 days, see below.
Risk: unknown

Activity
  4 forks (3.5 per 1,000 stars)
  0 watchers
  0 issues and pull requests in the last 90 days
  In StarTrust's comparison of 182 organic repos, every one had at least 10
  forks per 1,000 stars. Watchers and issues vary a lot with the kind of repo.
  But most repos flagged for bought stars also had normal numbers here, so
  normal numbers do not prove that the stars are real. Few forks alone also mean
  nothing, because tools such as `composer thanks` star library repos
  automatically.

Limits
- Anyone can star any repo, so a pattern here says nothing about who arranged
  it.
- GitHub only counts stars that still exist. Stars from deleted accounts are
  missing from the history.
- The accounts were not checked (--no-archive), so the verdict rests on the
  timing of the stars.

Checked <time> using 6 GitHub requests. Used no GitHub token, 60
requests an hour. Add --details for the full evidence.
